/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/022-hybrid-rag-fusion/009-perfect-session-capturing/016-json-mode-hybrid-enrichment/003-field-integrity-and-schema/spec.md:26:The `generate-context.js` pipeline contains two categories of correctness gap discovered during deep research Round 2 (74 findings, 20 recommendations). Domain A is a data-loss defect: when an AI sends both `userPrompts` (triggering the fast path) and `filesModified`, the file listing is silently discarded. Domain B is a set of five schema and validation weaknesses that allow typo'd fields, over-long strings, invalid enum values, malformed YAML frontmatter, and trivially short content to pass through to storage undetected. Together these eight changes harden the pipeline against both accidental data loss and silent quality degradation.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/022-hybrid-rag-fusion/009-perfect-session-capturing/016-json-mode-hybrid-enrichment/003-field-integrity-and-schema/spec.md:55:The `generate-context.js` pipeline has a split code path in `input-normalizer.ts` (lines 414-530): a fast path triggered by `userPrompts`, `observations`, or `recentContext`, and a slow path for all other inputs. The fast path converts 11 field families but omits the `filesModified` -> `FILES` conversion that exists only on the slow path (lines 504-529). When an AI sends `filesModified` alongside any fast-path trigger field, the file listing is silently lost with no warning emitted. Separately, `RawInputData` uses a `[key: string]: unknown` index signature, meaning typo'd field names (e.g. `sesionSummary`) are accepted and silently dropped; `contextType` accepts any string despite the type-system defining an enum; string fields have no length cap; frontmatter is validated via fragile regex rather than a real parser; and quality flags `duplicate_observations` and `short_content` exist but no V-rule enforces them.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/022-hybrid-rag-fusion/009-perfect-session-capturing/016-json-mode-hybrid-enrichment/003-field-integrity-and-schema/spec.md:232:**As an** AI assistant saving a memory via `generate-context.js`, **I want** my `filesModified` list to appear in the saved memory regardless of whether I also sent `userPrompts`, **so that** the memory accurately reflects which files were touched in the session.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/022-hybrid-rag-fusion/009-perfect-session-capturing/016-json-mode-hybrid-enrichment/003-field-integrity-and-schema/plan.md:35:Eight changes across two files harden the `generate-context.js` pipeline against data loss and silent schema violations. The P0 change adds a `filesModified` -> `FILES` conversion to the fast path in `input-normalizer.ts`, mirroring the existing slow-path conversion. The P1 changes add unknown-field warnings, `contextType` enum validation, string length limits, a YAML parser replacement, and a content density V-rule. The P2 changes add V12 path normalization and a status/percentage contradiction V-rule. No public interfaces change; all additions are internal guards.

/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/022-hybrid-rag-fusion/009-perfect-session-capturing/016-json-mode-hybrid-enrichment/004-indexing-and-coherence/spec.md:3:description: "Four domains of the generate-context.js pipeline are degraded: embedding retry stats are invisible to operators, trigger phrase extraction produces 15-30 noisy phrases per memory that pollute binary matching, 15+ AI-composed fields are silently discarded by the template renderer, and cross-session deduplication is AI-dependent with zero automated verification of referenced memory IDs or causal links."
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/022-hybrid-rag-fusion/009-perfect-session-capturing/016-json-mode-hybrid-enrichment/004-indexing-and-coherence/spec.md:23:Four structural gaps in the generate-context.js memory pipeline degrade indexing quality and cross-session coherence without surfacing any observable errors. Embedding retry failures are silently tracked by a background job but never exposed through MCP tooling, leaving operators blind to vector-search degradation. Trigger phrase extraction produces 15-30 noisy phrases per memory dominated by path fragments and n-gram shingles, causing binary trigger matching to return low-quality results. The Mustache template renderer silently discards 15+ AI-composed fields (toolCalls, exchanges, pipeline flags), while 8 phantom V2.2 placeholders are always empty and 9 valid data-source bindings are suppressed. Cross-session dedup is purely AI-assisted: referenced memory IDs are never validated, causal links receive no graph verification, and observation arrays are deduped only within a single render pass.
/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/022-hybrid-rag-fusion/009-perfect-session-capturing/016-json-mode-hybrid-enrichment/004-indexing-and-coherence/spec.md:54:The generate-context.js pipeline has no observable signal for embedding health: the retry manager runs a background job every 5 minutes with circuit-breaker logic, but its RetryStats object (pending count, failed count, retry attempts, circuit breaker state) never reaches any MCP tool. Operators using `memory_health` cannot distinguish "all embeddings healthy" from "all embeddings stuck with circuit breaker open." Separately, the trigger phrase system's n-gram auto-extraction (depth 4) produces 15-30 phrases per memory that include raw path fragments ("system spec kit/022 hybrid rag fusion"), single-word shingles, and generic tokens under 3 characters — these dilute the manually authored phrases that survive the RC2 fix (workflow.ts:978-988) and flood binary trigger matching with score=1.0 false positives. On the template rendering side, `toolCalls` (ToolCallSummary[]) and `exchanges` (ExchangeSummary[]) from CollectedDataBase are never bound to any Mustache section; the data is AI-composed and ingested but silently falls off the render path, permanently discarded. Eight V2.2 placeholder tokens in template-renderer.ts OPTIONAL_PLACEHOLDERS have no construction sites anywhere in the codebase, guaranteeing empty output, while 9 other suppressed OPTIONAL_PLACEHOLDERs now have active data sources (buildMemoryClassificationContext, buildSessionDedupContext) that are masked by stale suppression logic. Finally, cross-session coherence has no automated layer: buildSessionDedupContext() computes a SHA1 fingerprint but never queries existing memories to detect overlaps, similar_memories references from AI input pass through with no ID validation, causal link types are accepted without graph-level verification, and observation deduplication only runs within a single render pass.

Keep this pass at the R-05 recommended boundary: - Add `CHOICE_CONFIDENCE` and `RATIONALE_CONFIDENCE` - Keep legacy `CONFIDENCE = Math.min(choice, rationale)` for compatibility - Update decision rendering to show the split signal - Do **not** redefine high/medium/low counts or importance logic yet; they continue to use derived legacy `CONFIDENCE` ## Public Interfaces / Types - Extend `DecisionRecord` in `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/types/session-types.ts` with: - `CHOICE_CONFIDENCE: number` - `RATIONALE_CONFIDENCE: number` - keep `CONFIDENCE: number` required - Extend `DecisionNode` in `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/lib/decision-tree-generator.ts` to optionally accept the two new fields. - Preserve the current normalized range contract: all three confidence fields are `0.0-1.0` in extractor output; percentage conversion remains a render/workflow concern. ## Implementation Changes - In the decision extractor, factor confidence calculation into one shared helper used by both manual and observation-derived decisions. - Compute choice confidence with this fixed rule: - base `0.50` - `+0.15` when 2+ alternatives/options exist - `+0.10` when an explicit choice is present (`chosen`, `choice`, `selected`, parsed chosen phrase, or `_manualDecision.chosenApproach`) - `+0.10` when the chosen option is specific, not a placeholder like `Chosen Approach` or `N/A` - cap at `1.0` - Compute rationale confidence with this fixed rule: - base `0.50` - `+0.15` when explicit rationale/reasoning text exists beyond the generic fallback snippet - `+0.10` when trade-off language exists (pros/cons, advantages/disadvantages, caveats) - `+0.10` when supporting evidence exists (file evidence or fact evidence) - cap at `1.0` - When legacy single-value confidence is explicitly supplied (`_manualDecision.confidence` or `confidence:` in narrative), treat it as an override for **both** new fields after normalization/clamping; then derive legacy `CONFIDENCE` from those equal values. - Recompute `CONFIDENCE` everywhere decisions are created as `Math.min(CHOICE_CONFIDENCE, RATIONALE_CONFIDENCE)`. - Keep `HIGH_CONFIDENCE_COUNT`, `MEDIUM_CONFIDENCE_COUNT`, `LOW_CONFIDENCE_COUNT`, and `DECISION_IMPORTANCE` based on derived `CONFIDENCE` in this phase. - Update decision rendering surfaces only where they actually exist in the live repo: - `decision-tree-generator.ts` and `ascii-boxes.ts` should show split confidence when the values differ by more than `0.10`, otherwise keep the single confidence display - `templates/context_template.md` should render `Choice: X% / Rationale: Y%` for divergent values and the existing single confidence line otherwise - `workflow.ts` should continue converting normalized values to percentages for template input, and should pass the new percentage fields alongside legacy `CONFIDENCE` - Update simulation/fixture producers so generated decision objects include the new fields and still satisfy the old contract. - Do not change `validate-memory-quality.ts` logic unless a rendered-output fixture requires a minimal adjustment; the live validator is not a real consumer of decision confidence semantics. - After code verification, update the phase docs in `005-confidence-calibration/`: - mark tasks/checklist items with evidence - write `implementation-summary.md` - save context via `node.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/dist/memory/generate-context.js ` ## Test Plan - Add a focused unit suite for dual-confidence extraction cases, preferably a new `scripts/tests/decision-confidence.vitest.ts`, covering: - alternatives only - rationale only - strong choice / weak rationale - weak choice / strong rationale - explicit single confidence override - clamping and normalization - legacy `CONFIDENCE === Math.min(choice, rationale)` - Update existing regression suites to reflect the new shape without breaking backward compatibility: - `scripts/tests/test-extractors-loaders.js` - `scripts/tests/test-scripts-modules.js` - `scripts/tests/memory-render-fixture.vitest.ts` - `scripts/lib/simulation-factory.ts` fixture expectations - Verification commands: - `npm run typecheck` - `node mcp_server/node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/decision-confidence.vitest.ts tests/memory-render-fixture.vitest.ts --root scripts --config../mcp_server/vitest.config.ts` - `node scripts/tests/test-extractors-loaders.js` - `node scripts/tests/test-scripts-modules.js` - `scripts/spec/validate.sh ` ## Assumptions - The live implementation target is `.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/...`; phase docs that reference top-level `scripts/...` are descriptive but not the real file layout. - `DecisionRecord` is already canonical enough for this phase despite `004-type-consolidation` docs still showing draft status. - This phase intentionally defers split analytics/counting beyond rendering and extractor enrichment, per the R-05 recommendation and your selected scope.

This is not a simple “change the root path” patch. The implementation should: - normalize backend-native paths into a shared `.opencode` workspace identity, - stop relying on raw absolute-path equality across CLIs, - prevent false `V7`/`V8` aborts caused by incomplete stateless normalization, - re-baseline `M-007` so it reflects actual shipped behavior instead of stale assumptions. ## Key Changes ### 1. Canonical workspace identity - Add a shared workspace-identity helper that derives the canonical target from the nearest repo-local `.opencode` directory. - The helper should produce an equivalence set for the active workspace, including: - the canonical `.opencode` path, - the enclosing repo root when `.opencode` is nested inside it, - normalized absolute forms used by CLI artifacts. - Replace direct project-root equality checks in native extractors with “same workspace identity” matching. - Keep `.opencode` as the source of truth; repo-root and git-root matches are accepted only when they resolve to the same workspace identity. ### 2. Backend matcher updates - Update `OpenCode`, `Claude`, `Codex`, `Copilot`, and `Gemini` capture discovery to use the shared identity helper before accepting a transcript/workspace/session. - Preserve existing backend-specific safety rules: - exact session selection preference where available, - reasoning/thought stripping, - in-project file filtering, - no cross-workspace opportunistic matching. - Make loader precedence unchanged conceptually, but evaluated after canonical identity normalization. ### 3. Stateless normalization and validation fixes - Fix stateless `TOOL_COUNT` derivation so `V7` is based on actual structured tool evidence, not just `FILES.length`. - Extend normalized capture shaping so read/search/bash-heavy sessions do not render execution artifacts while still reporting `tool_count: 0`. - Tighten prompt/exchange relevance fallback so lack of keyword match does not blindly re-include foreign-spec prompt text and trip `V8`. - Keep contamination blocking strict, but ensure valid captures for the active `.opencode` workspace are not rejected due to fallback pollution. ### 4. Manual validation and documentation truth - Update `M-007` so it explicitly states that native capture targets the repo-local `.opencode` workspace identity. - Rewrite `M-007b`, `M-007c`, and `M-007e` through `M-007i` expectations to match the corrected pipeline: - thin JSON fixture must be defined so it truly falls below threshold if abort is still intended, - alignment scenario must account for earlier gate precedence, - precedence means “first matching backend chosen,” not “first backend always yields a successful save.” - Refresh the feature catalog entry so “exact project match” is restated as “exact canonical workspace identity match via `.opencode` normalization.” - Update spec `010` evidence/acceptance text to separate: - discovery precedence, - capture normalization, - final save/index success. ## Public Interfaces / Types - Add a shared internal workspace-identity utility used by extractors and loader-facing matching. - No CLI signature changes for `generate-context.js`. - No change to JSON-mode authority semantics. - `DataSource` values remain the same. - Matching semantics change internally from raw absolute-path equality to canonical `.opencode` workspace equivalence. ## Test Plan 1. Add focused unit coverage for the workspace-identity helper. - `.opencode` path matches itself - repo root matches the same `.opencode` - git root matches the same `.opencode` - unrelated repo with a different `.opencode` is rejected - normalized symlink/trailing-slash variants remain equivalent 2. Expand extractor tests for each backend. - session accepted when artifact stores repo root but active canonical workspace is `.opencode` - session accepted when artifact stores `.opencode` - unrelated workspace rejected even if basename is similar - thought/reasoning stripping remains intact 3. Expand stateless normalization/validation tests. - `V7` no longer fires for tool-rich captures with sparse `FILES` - `V8` no longer fires because of fallback-to-all-prompt contamination when spec relevance is missing - thin JSON fixture either: - truly aborts below threshold, or - is reclassified as allowed and the docs are updated accordingly 4. Re-run the full closure stack. - `npm run lint` - `npm run build` - targeted Vitest suite for session capture, runtime memory inputs, stateless enrichment, and scorer calibration - JS regression suites - alignment drift - `spec/validate.sh` for `009-perfect-session-capturing` 5. Re-run `M-007` manually against the corrected runtime with no in-memory root override. - `M-007a` rich JSON authority - `M-007b` corrected thin-fixture expectation - `M-007c` mis-scoped stateless scenario - `M-007d` provenance-tagged enrichment - `M-007e` through `M-007i` backend precedence under canonical `.opencode` identity - `M-007j` empty-home `NO_DATA_AVAILABLE` ## Assumptions and Defaults - The user-approved contract is that repo-local `.opencode` is the only canonical workspace identity. - Repo root, git root, and backend-native stored paths are compatibility forms, not primary identifiers. - Documentation should be updated in place in the existing feature catalog entry and `M-007`, not split into new parallel docs. - If thin JSON still scores above threshold after the identity fixes, the playbook must be corrected rather than forcing an artificial abort rule that conflicts with shipped scorer behavior.

The fix keeps `.opencode` as the canonical workspace identity and keeps the fallback order unchanged, but makes workspace match only the first gate, not proof of spec relevance. ## Key Changes ### 1. Add a spec-affinity gate after backend discovery - Keep workspace-identity matching exactly as the backend discovery contract. - Add a second stateless alignment check in the workflow that requires at least one spec-specific anchor beyond “same workspace”. - Treat these as valid anchors: - a hit on a file declared in the target spec’s files-to-change table or spec-folder docs, - an exact spec id / slug mention in prompts, observations, or tool metadata, - strong keyword evidence derived from the target spec title/slug plus captured content. - Do not count generic `.opencode`, repo-root, or shared infrastructure paths as sufficient alignment. - If a stateless capture has no spec-specific anchor, throw `ALIGNMENT_BLOCK` before enrichment or indexing, even when the backend session belongs to the same workspace. - For explicit stateless saves, low alignment must no longer degrade to warning-only proceed in non-interactive mode. ### 2. Preserve real backend evidence so quality fails for the right reason - Expand stateless relevance filtering so tool calls survive when they are relevant through aligned exchange text, tool args, or tool output, not just file paths or short titles. - Keep `_toolCallCount` based on surviving structured tool evidence even when no `FILES` entry is produced. - Build richer tool observation titles from tool name plus target/action summary so the rendered memory is less repetitive and more semantically useful. - Generate `recentContext`, summary seed text, and observation carry-through only from exchanges that passed spec relevance, instead of letting generic session residue shape the final memory. - Preserve current rule meanings: - `V7` should only fire on genuinely contradictory tool state, not because rich tool evidence was dropped during normalization. - `V8` should continue to hard-fail foreign-spec-dominated captures. ### 3. Lock expected backend behavior - `OpenCode`: unrelated same-workspace infrastructure sessions must fail alignment and never index. - `Claude`: rich but foreign-spec transcripts remain expected `V8` failures. - `Codex`: tool-rich, file-sparse sessions must retain enough evidence to avoid false `V7`. - `Copilot` and `Gemini`: thin sessions remain expected quality failures unless they contain enough aligned prompt/tool/file evidence to pass honestly. - Discovery precedence stays `OpenCode -> Claude -> Codex -> Copilot -> Gemini -> NO_DATA_AVAILABLE`, but save success still depends on alignment and quality. ## Public Interfaces / Types - No CLI signature changes for `generate-context.js`. - No change to JSON-mode authority or the existing `DataSource` values. - Add one shared internal “spec-affinity” evaluator used by the workflow and alignment path. - Keep failure surface explicit and stable: mis-scoped captures fail with `ALIGNMENT_BLOCK`; low-signal or contaminated captures fail with `QUALITY_GATE_ABORT`. ## Test Plan - Add deterministic regression coverage for: - same-workspace but off-spec OpenCode capture hard-failing `ALIGNMENT_BLOCK`, - Codex tool-rich / sparse-file capture rendering non-zero tool evidence and not false-failing `V7`, - Claude foreign-spec capture still hard-failing `V8`, - thin Copilot and Gemini captures failing quality without indexing, - no change to workspace-identity equivalence or backend fallback order. - Update the existing targeted Vitest suites around runtime memory inputs, stateless enrichment, backend extractors, and memory-render fixtures to encode those cases directly. - Re-run the existing verification stack: - `npm run lint` - `npm run build` - targeted Vitest session-capture suite - JS extractor / integration / bug-fix / memory-quality suites - alignment drift - `spec/validate.sh` for `009-perfect-session-capturing` - Re-run `M-007` with tightened expectations: - `M-007c` must hard-fail for mis-scoped same-workspace sessions, - `M-007e` must prove OpenCode discovery does not imply save success, - `M-007g` must prove Codex no longer false-fails `V7`, - `M-007h` and `M-007i` must record thin-session failure as expected unless the artifact is genuinely rich enough. ## Assumptions and Defaults - `.opencode` remains the canonical workspace identity anchor. - The user wants stricter false-positive prevention over permissive salvage for same-workspace captures. - Same-workspace generic infrastructure activity is not acceptable evidence for saving into a specific spec folder. - The right fix is to improve normalization for valid rich captures while making unrelated and low-signal captures fail earlier and more explicitly, not to lower the quality/alignment bars.

The new rule is: - good memories save - off-spec memories still fail alignment/contamination as they do now - thin, under-evidenced, or metadata-only memories fail with a new explicit `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` - this hard-block applies everywhere: native capture, explicit JSON, and MCP `memory_save` This plan keeps `.opencode` workspace identity and the existing fallback order, but stops treating a spec anchor, long rendered output, or auto-generated metadata as sufficient proof of memory quality. ## Key Changes ### 1. Add one shared memory-sufficiency evaluator - Introduce a shared internal module that evaluates a normalized evidence snapshot instead of relying on backend-specific heuristics. - The evaluator should return: - `pass` - `rejectionCode: 'INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT'` - `reasons` - `evidenceCounts` - `score` or normalized sufficiency value for diagnostics - Use the same pass contract across all platforms: - specific title is required - at least 1 primary evidence item is required - at least 2 total spec-relevant evidence items are required - semantic substance is required: minimum aligned text floor such as `>=250` semantic chars or `>=40` unique words - Count as primary evidence only: - meaningful file role with non-placeholder description - meaningful tool result tied to the target task/spec - concrete decision / next action / blocker / outcome - substantive observation with a non-generic title and useful narrative - Count as support evidence only: - additional aligned prompt or exchange - anchored section structure - trigger phrases that are not generic - recent context with specific request/learning - Do not count: - workspace match by itself - generic titles like `session`, `development session`, `update` - placeholder file descriptions - single anchored prompts with no other substance - synthetic/provenance enrichment unless it is clearly target-spec-specific ### 2. Harden `generate-context.js` and the native/JSON pipeline - Run the new sufficiency gate after stateless enrichment and relevance filtering, before file writing or indexing. - Apply it to: - `OpenCode` - `Claude Code` - `Codex CLI` - `Copilot CLI` - `Gemini CLI` - explicit JSON input - Keep failure types distinct: - off-spec or same-workspace wrong task: `ALIGNMENT_BLOCK` - foreign-spec dominated content: existing contamination/quality failure path (`V8`) - not enough real context even though aligned: `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` - Tighten normalization so backend evidence survives when it is real: - preserve meaningful tool outputs - preserve file-role hints - preserve decision/next-step evidence - keep single-message anchored sessions from being inflated into valid memories - Keep the legacy 0-100 scorer for diagnostics only. - Keep v2 `quality_score` metadata, but make it reflect insufficiency strongly so thin memories score low instead of looking healthy. ### 3. Apply the same rule to MCP `memory_save` - Add the shared sufficiency gate to the server-side save path in the common handler flow, not as a session-capture-only rule. - Run order should be: 1. parse/validate 2. quality-loop auto-fixes for recoverable formatting only 3. shared sufficiency gate 4. embedding / dedup / persistence - The quality loop must not try to “repair” semantic insufficiency by inventing context. - `force: true` must not override insufficient-context rejection. - `dryRun: true` must surface the insufficiency result with reasons and evidence counts, with no write/index side effects. - The new insufficiency rejection must hard-block immediately and must not respect the older warn-only rollout behavior from the save-quality gate. ### 4. Align scoring, responses, and docs - Add a stable explicit failure contract everywhere: - CLI/runtime errors include `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` - MCP save responses include `rejectionCode` and insufficiency details - Update server response builders and recovery hints so the user/agent sees “not enough context for a proper memory” instead of a vague generic quality failure. - Refresh the canonical docs in place: - `009-perfect-session-capturing` for capture-entry behavior - `NEW-139` feature-catalog entry - pre-storage quality gate feature doc - quality-loop feature doc - dry-run preflight feature doc - manual playbook scenarios for both capture and `memory_save` ## Public Interfaces / Types - New shared internal type such as `MemorySufficiencyResult` / `MemoryEvidenceSnapshot`. - New stable failure code: `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT`. - `generate-context.js` CLI signature does not change, but its error contract expands to include the new failure code. - `memory_save` response should add explicit insufficiency reporting, including `rejectionCode` and structured reasons/evidence. - No backend-specific save thresholds; all platforms use the same sufficiency contract after their evidence is normalized. ## Test Plan - Add direct unit coverage for the shared sufficiency evaluator: - rich specific evidence passes - single anchored prompt fails - generic title plus long content fails - placeholder file descriptions do not count - spec-specific tool output can satisfy primary evidence - Expand session-capture tests for: - same-workspace off-spec OpenCode still `ALIGNMENT_BLOCK` - rich Codex capture passes and no longer false-fails - foreign-spec Claude capture still fails the existing contamination path - thin but anchored Copilot and Gemini captures fail `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` - thin explicit JSON fails `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` - rich explicit JSON still passes - Expand MCP save tests for: - `memory_save({ dryRun: true })` returns explicit insufficiency result - normal save rejects insufficient memories before embedding/storage - `force: true` does not bypass the new gate - quality-loop fixes formatting issues but cannot rescue semantic insufficiency - warn-only quality-gate behavior does not bypass the new insufficiency hard block - Re-run the relevant automated stacks: - scripts lint/build/Vitest/JS suites - MCP server quality-gate, quality-loop, memory-save, and preflight suites - alignment drift - spec validation - Rework manual testing so it proves: - rich JSON/native saves still pass honestly - thin aligned saves fail explicitly - all five native backends behave consistently - `memory_save` dry-run and real save both notice insufficient context ## Assumptions And Defaults - “All platforms” means all five native CLI backends, explicit JSON input, and MCP `memory_save`. - The new `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` is immediate and authoritative everywhere. - `force` can bypass dedup/update constraints when already supported, but not alignment, contamination, or insufficient-context gates. - The implementation should reuse existing docs where possible instead of creating parallel feature-catalog entries unless a validator or taxonomy rule requires one.

Additionally, when saving from Claude Code (or any external CLI), the script's session capture detects the active OpenCode editor session instead of the calling session, leading to ALIGNMENT_BLOCK rejections or saving the wrong session's context. Root cause investigation traced these to bugs in `scripts/core/workflow.ts` and `templates/context_template.md`. --- ## Root Cause Analysis ### BUG 1: ANCHOR tags destroyed by HTML comment stripping (CRITICAL) **Location:** `workflow.ts:108,162-179,1360-1364` **Chain of events:** 1. Template `context_template.md` contains 26 ANCHOR tags: `<!-- ANCHOR:id -->` / `<!-- /ANCHOR:id -->` 2. Step 8 (`populateTemplate`) renders the template correctly, anchors intact 3. Step 8.5 calls `stripWorkflowHtmlOutsideCodeFences()` on the rendered output 4. That function uses `WORKFLOW_HTML_COMMENT_RE = //g` (line 108) 5. This regex matches **all** HTML comments, including every ANCHOR tag 6. Line 171: `.replace(WORKFLOW_HTML_COMMENT_RE, '')` — deletes them all 7. Result: 0 ANCHOR tags in output file **Irony:** Line 538 has `extractAnchorIds()` that parses ANCHOR tags — but it runs after they've been destroyed. **Fix:** Modify the HTML comment regex to exclude ANCHOR comments: ```typescript // Before (line 108): const WORKFLOW_HTML_COMMENT_RE = /<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g; // After: const WORKFLOW_HTML_COMMENT_RE = /<!--(?!\s*\/?ANCHOR:)[\s\S]*?-->/g; ``` The negative lookahead `(?!\s*\/?ANCHOR:)` preserves `<!-- ANCHOR:id -->` and `<!-- /ANCHOR:id -->` while still stripping all other HTML comments. ### BUG 2: Frontmatter trigger_phrases are hardcoded (HIGH) **Location:** `templates/context_template.md:4-7` vs `templates/context_template.md:807-811` **Chain of events:** 1. Template frontmatter (lines 4-7) has static values: ```yaml trigger_phrases: - "memory dashboard" - "session summary" - "context template" ``` 2. The ` system spec kit/022 hybrid rag fusion/010 perfect session capturing, dry run, rejection code, no data available, memory_save, json mode, repo local, save path, target spec, tool call, current spec, auto fixes, warn only, save quality, under evidenced, hard blocks, post render, tree thinning, implementation summary, merged-small-files tree-thinning merged small, tree-thinning merged small files, one shared semantic sufficiency, evidence the workflow, cleanup the workflow, keep one ordered native, one ordered native fallback, system, spec, kit/022, hybrid, rag, fusion/010, perfect, session, capturing` mustache variable IS used — but only in the YAML metadata block at line 807-811 (inside the trailing ```` ```yaml ```` code fence) 3. The workflow DOES extract session-specific triggers (`preExtractedTriggers`, line 1231-1269) and passes them as `TRIGGER_PHRASES` to the template (line 1315) 4. But the frontmatter section never references ` system spec kit/022 hybrid rag fusion/010 perfect session capturing, dry run, rejection code, no data available, memory_save, json mode, repo local, save path, target spec, tool call, current spec, auto fixes, warn only, save quality, under evidenced, hard blocks, post render, tree thinning, implementation summary, merged-small-files tree-thinning merged small, tree-thinning merged small files, one shared semantic sufficiency, evidence the workflow, cleanup the workflow, keep one ordered native, one ordered native fallback, system, spec, kit/022, hybrid, rag, fusion/010, perfect, session, capturing` — it uses hardcoded strings **Fix:** Replace the static frontmatter trigger_phrases with the template variable: ```yaml # Before (lines 4-7): trigger_phrases: - "memory dashboard" - "session summary" - "context template" # After: trigger_phrases: {{#TRIGGER_PHRASES}} - "" {{/TRIGGER_PHRASES}}  ``` ### BUG 3: Cross-session contamination — ALREADY FIXED by 010 Spec `009-perfect-session-capturing` (completed 2026-03-15) already addresses this via: - Canonical `.opencode` workspace identity normalization (`workspace-identity.ts`) - Target-spec affinity gate (`spec-affinity.ts`) requiring anchor match beyond workspace - `ALIGNMENT_BLOCK` hard-fail for same-workspace off-spec sessions - `INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT_ABORT` for under-evidenced memories - Safe prompt fallback that drops foreign-spec content **No additional fix needed.** The remaining quality gap (JSON fallback producing lower-quality saves) is by design — JSON mode lacks native session data.     71	    if (typeof text === 'string') {
    72	      const parsed = JSON.parse(text);
    73	      return parsed?.data ?? parsed ?? {};

    75	  } catch { /* parse failed */ }
    76	  return {};
    77	}

    85	  data: Record<string, unknown>,

    88	  if (candidate && typeof candidate === 'object') {
    89	    return candidate as CachedSessionSummaryDecision;
    90	  }
    91	  return null;
    92	}

    95	  resumeData: Record<string, unknown>,
    96	  healthData: Record<string, unknown>,
    97	  structuralContext: StructuralBootstrapContract,
    98	): string[] {
    99	  const nextActions = new Set<string>();
   100	
   101	  if (resumeData.error) {
   102	    nextActions.add('Call `session_resume({ specFolder })` directly to inspect the detailed resume failure.');
   103	  }

   106	    nextActions.add('Call `session_health()` directly to inspect the current health-check failure.');
   107	  }

   112

   115	  } else if (structuralContext.status === 'stale') {

   117	  } else {

   124	  }

   131	): StructuralTrust | null {
   132	  if (!payload) {
   133	    return null;
   134	  }
   135	
   136	  const structuralSection = payload.sections.find((section) =>
   137	    section.key === 'structural-context' && section.structuralTrust,
   138	  );
   139	
   140	  return structuralSection?.structuralTrust ?? null;
   141	}
   142	
   143	function buildStructuralRoutingNudge(
   144	  structuralContext: StructuralBootstrapContract,
   145	): SessionBootstrapResult['structuralRoutingNudge'] | null {
   146	  if (structuralContext.status !== 'ready') {
   147	    return null;
   148	  }
   149	
   150	  return {
   151	    advisory: true,
   152	    readiness: 'ready',

   155	    preservesAuthority: 'session_bootstrap',

   162	
   163	/** Handle session_bootstrap tool call — one-call session setup */
   164	export async function handleSessionBootstrap(args: SessionBootstrapArgs): Promise<MCPResponse> {
   165	  const startMs = Date.now();
   166	  const allHints: string[] = [];
   167

   175	    allHints.push(...extractHints(resumeData));

   178	    resumeData = { error: message };
   179	    allHints.push('session_resume failed. Try calling it manually.');
   180	  }

   182	  // Sub-call 2: session_health

   187	    allHints.push(...extractHints(healthData));
   188	  } catch (error: unknown) {
   189	    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
   190	    healthData = { error: message };
   191	    allHints.push('session_health failed. Try calling it manually.');
   192	  }

   196	  if (structuralContext.status === 'stale' || structuralContext.status === 'missing') {

   207	  if (structuralRoutingNudge) {
   208	    allHints.push(structuralRoutingNudge.message);
   209	  }
   210	
   211	  // Deduplicate hints
   212	  const uniqueHints = [...new Set(allHints)];
   213	
   214	  // Record bootstrap telemetry once for the composite call.
   215	  const durationMs = Date.now() - startMs;
   216	  const completeness = resumeData.error || healthData.error ? 'partial' : 'full';
   217	  recordBootstrapEvent('tool', durationMs, completeness);
   218	
   219	  const resumeCertainty: SharedPayloadCertainty = resumeData.error ? 'unknown' : 'estimated';
   220	  const healthCertainty: SharedPayloadCertainty = healthData.error ? 'unknown' : 'estimated';

   555	        error: 'Cursor is invalid, expired, or out of scope',

   104	const memoryProtocolMarkdown = `## Engram Persistent Memory — Protocol
   105	
   106	You have access to Engram, a persistent memory system that survives across sessions and compactions.
   107	
   108	### WHEN TO SAVE (mandatory — not optional)
   109	
   110	Call mem_save IMMEDIATELY after any of these:
   111	- Bug fix completed
   112	- Architecture or design decision made
   113	- Non-obvious discovery about the codebase
   114	- Configuration change or environment setup
   115	- Pattern established (naming, structure, convention)
   116	- User preference or constraint learned
   117	
   118	Format for mem_save:
   119	- **title**: Verb + what — short, searchable (e.g. "Fixed N+1 query in UserList", "Chose Zustand over Redux")
   120	- **type**: bugfix | decision | architecture | discovery | pattern | config | preference
   121	- **scope**: project (default) | personal
   122	- **topic_key** (optional, recommended for evolving decisions): stable key like architecture/auth-model
   123	- **content**:
   124	  **What**: One sentence — what was done
   125	  **Why**: What motivated it (user request, bug, performance, etc.)
   126	  **Where**: Files or paths affected
   127	  **Learned**: Gotchas, edge cases, things that surprised you (omit if none)
   128	
   129	### Topic update rules (mandatory)
   130	
   131	- Different topics must not overwrite each other (e.g. architecture vs bugfix)
   132	- Reuse the same topic_key to update an evolving topic instead of creating new observations
   133	- If unsure about the key, call mem_suggest_topic_key first and then reuse it
   134	- Use mem_update when you have an exact observation ID to correct
   135	
   136	### WHEN TO SEARCH MEMORY
   137	
   138	When the user asks to recall something — any variation of "remember", "recall", "what did we do",
   139	"how did we solve", "recordar", "acordate", "qué hicimos", or references to past work:
   140	1. First call mem_context — checks recent session history (fast, cheap)
   141	2. If not found, call mem_search with relevant keywords (FTS5 full-text search)
   142	3. If you find a match, use mem_get_observation for full untruncated content
   143	
   144	Also search memory PROACTIVELY when:
   145	- Starting work on something that might have been done before
   146	- The user mentions a topic you have no context on — check if past sessions covered it
   147	
   148	### SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL (mandatory)
   149	
   150	Before ending a session or saying "done" / "listo" / "that's it", you MUST:
   151	1. Call mem_session_summary with this structure:
   152	
   153	## Goal
   154	[What we were working on this session]
   155	
   156	## Instructions
   157	[User preferences or constraints discovered — skip if none]
   158	
   159	## Discoveries
   160	- [Technical findings, gotchas, non-obvious learnings]
   161	
   162	## Accomplished
   163	- [Completed items with key details]
   164	
   165	## Next Steps
   166	- [What remains to be done — for the next session]
   167	
   168	## Relevant Files
   169	- path/to/file — [what it does or what changed]
   170	
   171	This is NOT optional. If you skip this, the next session starts blind.
   172	
   173	### PASSIVE CAPTURE — automatic learning extraction
   174	
   175	When completing a task or subtask, include a "## Key Learnings:" section at the end of your response
   176	with numbered items. Engram will automatically extract and save these as observations.
   177	
   178	Example:
   179	## Key Learnings:
   180	
   181	1. bcrypt cost=12 is the right balance for our server performance
   182	2. JWT refresh tokens need atomic rotation to prevent race conditions
   183	
   184	You can also call mem_capture_passive(content) directly with any text that contains a learning section.
   185	This is a safety net — it captures knowledge even if you forget to call mem_save explicitly.
   186	
   187	### AFTER COMPACTION
   188	
   189	If you see a message about compaction or context reset, or if you see "FIRST ACTION REQUIRED" in your context:
   190	1. IMMEDIATELY call mem_session_summary with the compacted summary content — this persists what was done before compaction
   191	2. Then call mem_context to recover any additional context from previous sessions
   192	3. Only THEN continue working
   193	
   194	Do not skip step 1. Without it, everything done before compaction is lost from memory.
   195	`

   126	async function engramFetch(

   133	      headers: opts.body ? { "Content-Type": "application/json" } : undefined,
   134	      body: opts.body ? JSON.stringify(opts.body) : undefined,
   135	    })
   136	    return await res.json()
   137	  } catch {
   138	    // Engram server not running — silently fail
   139	    return null
   140	  }
   141	}

   164	        if (name) return name
   165	      }
   166	    }
   167	  } catch {}

   171	    const result = Bun.spawnSync(["git", "-C", directory, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"])
   172	    if (result.exitCode === 0) {

   174	      if (root) return root.split("/").pop() ?? "unknown"
   175	    }
   176	  } catch {}
   177	
   178	  // Final fallback: cwd basename
   179	  return directory.split("/").pop() ?? "unknown"
   180	}

     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Engram — SessionStart hook for Claude Code
     3	#
     4	# 1. Ensures the engram server is running
     5	# 2. Creates a session in engram
     6	# 3. Auto-imports git-synced chunks if .engram/manifest.json exists
     7	# 4. Injects Memory Protocol instructions + memory context
     8	
     9	ENGRAM_PORT="${ENGRAM_PORT:-7437}"
    10	ENGRAM_URL="http://127.0.0.1:${ENGRAM_PORT}"
    11	
    12	# Load shared helpers

    15	
    16	# Read hook input from stdin
    17	INPUT=$(cat)
    18	SESSION_ID=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.session_id // empty')
    19	CWD=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.cwd // empty')
    20	OLD_PROJECT=$(basename "$CWD")
    21	PROJECT=$(detect_project "$CWD")
    22	
    23	# Ensure engram server is running
    24	if ! curl -sf "${ENGRAM_URL}/health" --max-time 1 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    25	  engram serve &>/dev/null &
    26	  sleep 0.5
    27	fi
    28	
    29	# Migrate project name if it changed (one-time, idempotent)
    30	if [ "$OLD_PROJECT" != "$PROJECT" ] && [ -n "$OLD_PROJECT" ] && [ -n "$PROJECT" ]; then
    31	  curl -sf "${ENGRAM_URL}/projects/migrate" \
    32	    -X POST \
    33	    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    34	    -d "$(jq -n --arg old "$OLD_PROJECT" --arg new "$PROJECT" \
    35	      '{old_project: $old, new_project: $new}')" \
    36	    > /dev/null 2>&1
    37	fi
    38	
    39	# Create session
    40	if [ -n "$SESSION_ID" ] && [ -n "$PROJECT" ]; then
    41	  curl -sf "${ENGRAM_URL}/sessions" \
    42	    -X POST \
    43	    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    44	    -d "$(jq -n --arg id "$SESSION_ID" --arg project "$PROJECT" --arg dir "$CWD" \
    45	      '{id: $id, project: $project, directory: $dir}')" \
    46	    > /dev/null 2>&1
    47	fi
    48	
    49	# Auto-import git-synced chunks
    50	if [ -f "${CWD}/.engram/manifest.json" ]; then

    52	fi

   136	// Robustness: signal handler releases locks before reporting
   137	function handleSignalShutdown(signal: string): void {
   138	  if (shuttingDown) return; // prevent re-entrant handling
   139	  shuttingDown = true;
   140	
   141	  let lockReleaseFailed = false;
   142	  try {
   143	    releaseFilesystemLock();
   144	  } catch (_err: unknown) {
   145	    lockReleaseFailed = true;
   146	  }
   147	
   148	  console.error(`\nWarning: Received ${signal} signal, shutting down gracefully...`);
   149	  process.exit(lockReleaseFailed ? 1 : 0);
   150	}

   152	function installSignalHandlers(): void {
   153	  if (signalHandlersInstalled) {
   154	    return;
   155	  }
   156	
   157	  process.on('SIGTERM', () => handleSignalShutdown('SIGTERM'));
   158	  process.on('SIGINT', () => handleSignalShutdown('SIGINT'));
   159	
   160	  signalHandlersInstalled = true;
   161	}

   164	// 4. SPEC FOLDER VALIDATION
   165	// ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   166	function isUnderApprovedSpecsRoot(normalizedInput: string): boolean {
   167	  return validateFilePath(path.resolve(CONFIG.PROJECT_ROOT, normalizedInput), getSpecsDirectories()) !== null;
   168	}
   169	
   170	function isValidSpecFolder(folderPath: string): SpecFolderValidation {
   171	  const folderName = path.basename(folderPath);
   172	
   173	  // --- Subfolder support: parent/child format (e.g., "003-parent/121-child" or "02--cat/003-parent/121-child") ---
   174	  const normalizedInput = folderPath.replace(/\\/g, '/').replace(/\/+$/, '');
   175	  // Extract the trailing portion that might be "parent/child"
   176	  const trailingSegments = normalizedInput.split('/');
   177	  // Check if the last two segments both match the spec folder pattern
   178	  if (trailingSegments.length >= 2) {
   179	    const lastTwo = trailingSegments.slice(-2);
   180	    if (SPEC_FOLDER_PATTERN.test(lastTwo[0]) && SPEC_FOLDER_PATTERN.test(lastTwo[1])) {
   181	      // Both segments are valid spec folder names — valid nested spec folder
   182	      const hasSpecsParent = isUnderApprovedSpecsRoot(normalizedInput);
   183	
   184	      if (!hasSpecsParent) {
   185	        // Fallback: check if the path resolves to an existing directory under any specs root
   186	        for (const specsDir of getSpecsDirectories()) {
   187	          const candidate = path.join(specsDir, normalizedInput);
   188	          if (
   189	            !path.isAbsolute(normalizedInput) &&
   190	            fsSync.existsSync(candidate) &&
   191	            validateFilePath(candidate, getSpecsDirectories()) !== null
   192	          ) {
   193	            return { valid: true };
   194	          }
   195	        }
   196	        return {
   197	          valid: false,
   198	          reason: `Spec folder must be under specs/ or .opencode/specs/: ${folderPath}`
   199	        };
   200	      }
   201	      return { valid: true };
   202	    }
   203	  }
   204	
   205	  if (!SPEC_FOLDER_PATTERN.test(folderName)) {
   206	    if (/^\d{3}-/.test(folderName)) {
   207	      if (/[A-Z]/.test(folderName)) {
   208	        return { valid: false, reason: 'Spec folder name should be lowercase' };
   209	      }
   210	      if (/_/.test(folderName)) {
   211	        return { valid: false, reason: 'Spec folder name should use hyphens, not underscores' };
   212	      }
   213	      if (!/^[a-z]/.test(folderName.slice(4))) {
   214	        return { valid: false, reason: 'Spec folder name must start with a letter after the number prefix' };
   215	      }
   216	    }
   217	    return { valid: false, reason: 'Invalid spec folder format. Expected: NNN-feature-name' };
   218	  }
   219	
   220	  const hasSpecsParent = isUnderApprovedSpecsRoot(normalizedInput);

     5	<p align="center">
     6	  <strong>Persistent memory for AI coding agents</strong><br>
     7	  <em>Agent-agnostic. Single binary. Zero dependencies.</em>
     8	</p>
     9	
    10	<p align="center">
    11	  <a href="docs/INSTALLATION.md">Installation</a> &bull;
    12	  <a href="docs/AGENT-SETUP.md">Agent Setup</a> &bull;

    18	
    19	---
    20	
    21	> **engram** `/ˈen.ɡræm/` — *neuroscience*: the physical trace of a memory in the brain.
    22	
    23	Your AI coding agent forgets everything when the session ends. Engram gives it a brain.
    24	
    25	A **Go binary** with SQLite + FTS5 full-text search, exposed via CLI, HTTP API, MCP server, and an interactive TUI. Works with **any agent** that supports MCP — Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Codex, VS Code (Copilot), Antigravity, Cursor, Windsurf, or anything else.
    26	
    27	```
    28	Agent (Claude Code / OpenCode / Gemini CLI / Codex / VS Code / Antigravity / ...)
    29	    ↓ MCP stdio
    30	Engram (single Go binary)
    31	    ↓
    32	SQLite + FTS5 (~/.engram/engram.db)
    33	```
    34	
    35	## Quick Start
    36	
    37	### Install
    38	
    39	```bash
    40	brew install gentleman-programming/tap/engram
    41	```
    42	
    43	Windows, Linux, and other install methods → [docs/INSTALLATION.md](docs/INSTALLATION.md)
    44	
    45	### Setup Your Agent
    46	
    47	| Agent | One-liner |
    48	|-------|-----------|
    49	| Claude Code | `claude plugin marketplace add Gentleman-Programming/engram && claude plugin install engram` |
    50	| OpenCode | `engram setup opencode` |
    51	| Gemini CLI | `engram setup gemini-cli` |
    52	| Codex | `engram setup codex` |
    53	| VS Code | `code --add-mcp '{"name":"engram","command":"engram","args":["mcp"]}'` |
    54	| Cursor / Windsurf / Any MCP | See [docs/AGENT-SETUP.md](docs/AGENT-SETUP.md) |
    55	
    56	Full per-agent config, Memory Protocol, and compaction survival → [docs/AGENT-SETUP.md](docs/AGENT-SETUP.md)
    57	
    58	That's it. No Node.js, no Python, no Docker. **One binary, one SQLite file.**
    59	
    60	## How It Works
    61	
    62	```
    63	1. Agent completes significant work (bugfix, architecture decision, etc.)
    64	2. Agent calls mem_save → title, type, What/Why/Where/Learned
    65	3. Engram persists to SQLite with FTS5 indexing
    66	4. Next session: agent searches memory, gets relevant context
    67	```
    68	
    69	Full details on session lifecycle, topic keys, and memory hygiene → [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
    70	
    71	## MCP Tools
    72	
    73	| Tool | Purpose |
    74	|------|---------|
    75	| `mem_save` | Save observation |
    76	| `mem_update` | Update by ID |
    77	| `mem_delete` | Soft or hard delete |
    78	| `mem_suggest_topic_key` | Stable key for evolving topics |
    79	| `mem_search` | Full-text search |
    80	| `mem_session_summary` | End-of-session save |
    81	| `mem_context` | Recent session context |
    82	| `mem_timeline` | Chronological drill-in |
    83	| `mem_get_observation` | Full content by ID |
    84	| `mem_save_prompt` | Save user prompt |
    85	| `mem_stats` | Memory statistics |
    86	| `mem_session_start` | Register session start |
    87	| `mem_session_end` | Mark session complete |
    88	| `mem_capture_passive` | Extract learnings from text output |
    89	| `mem_merge_projects` | Merge project name variants (admin) |
    90	
    91	Full tool reference → [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#mcp-tools](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#mcp-tools)
    92	
    93	## Terminal UI
    94	
    95	```bash
    96	engram tui
    97	```

    99	<p align="center">
   100	<img src="assets/tui-dashboard.png" alt="TUI Dashboard" width="400" />

   107	
   108	## Git Sync
   109	
   110	Share memories across machines. Uses compressed chunks — no merge conflicts, no huge files.
   111	
   112	```bash
   113	engram sync                    # Export new memories as compressed chunk
   114	git add .engram/ && git commit -m "sync engram memories"
   115	engram sync --import           # On another machine: import new chunks
   116	engram sync --status           # Check sync status
   117	```
   118	
   119	Full sync documentation → [DOCS.md](DOCS.md)
   120	
   121	## CLI Reference
   122	
   123	| Command | Description |
   124	|---------|-------------|
   125	| `engram setup [agent]` | Install agent integration |
   126	| `engram serve [port]` | Start HTTP API (default: 7437) |
   127	| `engram mcp` | Start MCP server (stdio). Accepts `--project` or `ENGRAM_PROJECT` |
   128	| `engram tui` | Launch terminal UI |
   129	| `engram search <query>` | Search memories |
   130	| `engram save <title> <msg>` | Save a memory |
   131	| `engram timeline <obs_id>` | Chronological context |
   132	| `engram context [project]` | Recent session context |
   133	| `engram stats` | Memory statistics |
   134	| `engram export [file]` | Export to JSON |
   135	| `engram import <file>` | Import from JSON |
   136	| `engram sync` | Git sync export |
   137	| `engram projects list` | Show all projects with observation/session/prompt counts |
   138	| `engram projects consolidate` | Interactive merge of similar project names (`--all`, `--dry-run`) |
   139	| `engram projects prune` | Remove projects with 0 observations (`--dry-run`) |
   140	| `engram version` | Show version |

     3	# Architecture
     4	
     5	- [How It Works](#how-it-works)
     6	- [Session Lifecycle](#session-lifecycle)
     7	- [MCP Tools](#mcp-tools)
     8	- [Progressive Disclosure](#progressive-disclosure-3-layer-pattern)
     9	- [Memory Hygiene](#memory-hygiene)

    13	
    14	---
    15	
    16	## How It Works
    17	
    18	<p align="center">
    19	  <img src="../assets/agent-save.png" alt="Agent saving a memory via mem_save" width="800" />
    20	  <br />
    21	  <em>The agent proactively calls <code>mem_save</code> after significant work — structured, searchable, no noise.</em>
    22	</p>
    23	
    24	Engram trusts the **agent** to decide what's worth remembering — not a firehose of raw tool calls.
    25	
    26	### The Agent Saves, Engram Stores
    27	
    28	```
    29	1. Agent completes significant work (bugfix, architecture decision, etc.)
    30	2. Agent calls mem_save with a structured summary:
    31	   - title: "Fixed N+1 query in user list"
    32	   - type: "bugfix"
    33	   - content: What/Why/Where/Learned format
    34	3. Engram persists to SQLite with FTS5 indexing
    35	4. Next session: agent searches memory, gets relevant context
    36	```
    37	
    38	---
    39	
    40	## Session Lifecycle
    41	
    42	```
    43	Session starts → Agent works → Agent saves memories proactively
    44	                                    ↓
    45	Session ends → Agent writes session summary (Goal/Discoveries/Accomplished/Files)
    46	                                    ↓
    47	Next session starts → Previous session context is injected automatically
    48	```
    49	
    50	---
    51	
    52	## MCP Tools
    53	
    54	| Tool | Purpose |
    55	|------|---------|
    56	| `mem_save` | Save a structured observation (decision, bugfix, pattern, etc.) |
    57	| `mem_update` | Update an existing observation by ID |
    58	| `mem_delete` | Delete an observation (soft-delete by default, hard-delete optional) |
    59	| `mem_suggest_topic_key` | Suggest a stable `topic_key` for evolving topics before saving |
    60	| `mem_search` | Full-text search across all memories |
    61	| `mem_session_summary` | Save end-of-session summary |
    62	| `mem_context` | Get recent context from previous sessions |
    63	| `mem_timeline` | Chronological context around a specific observation |
    64	| `mem_get_observation` | Get full content of a specific memory |
    65	| `mem_save_prompt` | Save a user prompt for future context |
    66	| `mem_stats` | Memory system statistics |
    67	| `mem_session_start` | Register a session start |
    68	| `mem_session_end` | Mark a session as completed |
    69	| `mem_capture_passive` | Extract learnings from text output |
    70	| `mem_merge_projects` | Merge project name variants into canonical name (admin) |
    71	
    72	---
    73	
    74	## Progressive Disclosure (3-Layer Pattern)
    75	
    76	Token-efficient memory retrieval — don't dump everything, drill in:
    77	
    78	```
    79	1. mem_search "auth middleware"     → compact results with IDs (~100 tokens each)
    80	2. mem_timeline observation_id=42  → what happened before/after in that session
    81	3. mem_get_observation id=42       → full untruncated content
    82	```
    83	
    84	---
    85	
    86	## Memory Hygiene
    87	
    88	- `mem_save` now supports `scope` (`project` default, `personal` optional)
    89	- `mem_save` also supports `topic_key`; with a topic key, saves become upserts (same project+scope+topic updates the existing memory)
    90	- Exact dedupe prevents repeated inserts in a rolling window (hash + project + scope + type + title)
    91	- Duplicates update metadata (`duplicate_count`, `last_seen_at`, `updated_at`) instead of creating new rows
    92	- Topic upserts increment `revision_count` so evolving decisions stay in one memory
    93	- `mem_delete` uses soft-delete by default (`deleted_at`), with optional hard delete
    94	- `mem_search`, `mem_context`, recent lists, and timeline ignore soft-deleted observations
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	## Topic Key Workflow (Recommended)
    99	
   100	Use this when a topic evolves over time (architecture, long-running feature decisions, etc.):
   101	
   102	```text
   103	1. mem_suggest_topic_key(type="architecture", title="Auth architecture")
   104	2. mem_save(..., topic_key="architecture-auth-architecture")
   105	3. Later change on same topic -> mem_save(..., same topic_key)
   106	   => existing observation is updated (revision_count++)
   107	```
   108	
   109	Different topics should use different keys (e.g. `architecture/auth-model` vs `bug/auth-nil-panic`) so they never overwrite each other.
   110	
   111	`mem_suggest_topic_key` now applies a family heuristic for consistency across sessions:
   112	
   113	- `architecture/*` for architecture/design/ADR-like changes
   114	- `bug/*` for fixes, regressions, errors, panics
   115	- `decision/*`, `pattern/*`, `config/*`, `discovery/*`, `learning/*` when detected
   116	
   117	---
   118	
   119	## Project Structure
   120	
   121	```
   122	engram/
   123	├── cmd/engram/main.go              # CLI entrypoint
   124	├── internal/
   125	│   ├── store/store.go              # Core: SQLite + FTS5 + all data ops
   126	│   ├── server/server.go            # HTTP REST API (port 7437)
   127	│   ├── mcp/mcp.go                  # MCP stdio server (15 tools)
   128	│   ├── setup/setup.go              # Agent plugin installer (go:embed)
   129	│   ├── project/                     # Project name detection + similarity matching
   130	│   │   └── project.go              # DetectProject, FindSimilar, Levenshtein
   131	│   ├── sync/sync.go                # Git sync: manifest + compressed chunks
   132	│   └── tui/                        # Bubbletea terminal UI
   133	│       ├── model.go                # Screen constants, Model, Init()
   134	│       ├── styles.go               # Lipgloss styles (Catppuccin Mocha)
   135	│       ├── update.go               # Input handling, per-screen handlers
   136	│       └── view.go                 # Rendering, per-screen views
   137	├── plugin/
   138	│   ├── opencode/engram.ts          # OpenCode adapter plugin
   139	│   └── claude-code/                # Claude Code plugin (hooks + skill)
   140	│       ├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json
   141	│       ├── .mcp.json
   142	│       ├── hooks/hooks.json
   143	│       ├── scripts/                # session-start, post-compaction, subagent-stop, session-stop
   144	│       └── skills/memory/SKILL.md
   145	├── skills/                         # Contributor AI skills (repo-wide standards + Engram-specific guardrails)
   146	├── setup.sh                        # Links repo skills into .claude/.codex/.gemini (project-local)
   147	├── assets/                         # Screenshots and media
   148	├── DOCS.md                         # Full technical documentation
   149	├── CONTRIBUTING.md                 # Contribution workflow and standards
   150	├── go.mod
   151	└── go.sum
   152	```
   153	
   154	---
   155	
   156	## CLI Reference
   157	
   158	```
   159	engram setup [agent]      Install/setup agent integration (opencode, claude-code, gemini-cli, codex)
   160	engram serve [port]       Start HTTP API server (default: 7437)
   161	engram mcp                Start MCP server (stdio transport)
   162	engram tui                Launch interactive terminal UI
   163	engram search <query>     Search memories
   164	engram save <title> <msg> Save a memory
   165	engram timeline <obs_id>  Chronological context around an observation
   166	engram context [project]  Recent context from previous sessions
   167	engram stats              Memory statistics
   168	engram export [file]      Export all memories to JSON
   169	engram import <file>      Import memories from JSON
   170	engram sync               Export new memories as compressed chunk to .engram/
   171	engram sync --all         Export ALL projects (ignore directory-based filter)
   172	engram projects list      Show all projects with obs/session/prompt counts
   173	engram projects consolidate  Interactive merge of similar project names [--all] [--dry-run]
   174	engram projects prune     Remove projects with 0 observations [--dry-run]
   175	engram version            Show version
   176	```

# Iteration 001: ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW

## Focus
ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW: Scan repository structure, key directories, main entry points, README, and architecture docs. Map high-level components and data flow.

## Findings
### Finding 1: Engram is built as a store-centered hub with thin delivery surfaces
- **Source**: [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/cmd/engram/main.go#L113](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/cmd/engram/main.go#L113); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#L119](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#L119)
- **What it does**: `cmd/engram/main.go` dispatches every surface from one binary: `serve`, `mcp`, `tui`, `search`, `save`, `context`, `sync`, `setup`. The architecture doc matches that by making `internal/store/store.go` the core, with MCP, HTTP, sync, setup, and TUI as adapters around it.
- **Why it matters for us**: Public already has richer retrieval than Engram, but its memory system spans many MCP tools, scripts, hooks, and supporting subsystems. Engram’s clearer “one core store, many thin surfaces” boundary is a useful architecture lens for reducing wrapper drift.
- **Recommendation**: prototype later
- **Impact**: medium

### Finding 2: Engram explicitly separates agent-safe MCP tools from admin/curation tools
- **Source**: [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/mcp/mcp.go#L50](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/mcp/mcp.go#L50); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/mcp/mcp.go#L124](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/mcp/mcp.go#L124); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts#L878](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/tool-schemas.ts#L878); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/context-server.ts#L851](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/context-server.ts#L851)
- **What it does**: Engram defines `ProfileAgent` and `ProfileAdmin`, resolves them through `ResolveTools()`, and pairs that with “core” versus “deferred” tool instructions. Public currently exposes a flat `TOOL_DEFINITIONS` list from the server without an equivalent profile gate.
- **Why it matters for us**: This is a concrete answer to the “tool clutter” problem. Public has a much broader MCP surface, so profile-aware listing or wrapper-level profiles could reduce prompt noise and lower misuse risk without removing power-user tools.
- **Recommendation**: adopt now
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 3: Engram treats sessions, prompts, and summaries as first-class persisted objects
- **Source**: [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L441](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L441); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L754](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L754); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L1613](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L1613); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/mcp/mcp.go#L460](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/mcp/mcp.go#L460); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/session-resume.ts#L400](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/session-resume.ts#L400); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/session-bootstrap.ts#L163](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/session-bootstrap.ts#L163)
- **What it does**: Engram persists `sessions`, `observations`, and `user_prompts` as separate tables, exposes `mem_session_start`, `mem_session_end`, and `mem_session_summary`, then composes startup context by formatting recent sessions, prompts, and observations together. Public has strong resume/bootstrap orchestration, but it is centered on recovery composition rather than a lightweight explicit session-start/session-end API.
- **Why it matters for us**: Public is already stronger at startup recovery and structural readiness, but Engram’s explicit lifecycle tools would add a simpler durable narrative boundary around a session. That is especially useful for compaction survival and for cleaner prompt/session/history analytics.
- **Recommendation**: adopt now
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 4: Engram’s memory hygiene revolves around stable topic threads plus duplicate suppression
- **Source**: [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L948](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L948); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L3198](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L3198); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#L86](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#L86); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/memory/generate-context.ts#L75](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/scripts/memory/generate-context.ts#L75); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-save.ts#L1078](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-save.ts#L1078)
- **What it does**: `AddObservation()` first upserts on `topic_key + project + scope`, incrementing `revision_count`; if no topic match exists, it checks a rolling duplicate window and increments `duplicate_count` instead of inserting a new row. Public’s save path is file-first and quality-gated through `generate-context.ts` and `memory_save`, but it does not expose a comparable first-class thread-key convention for evolving topics.
- **Why it matters for us**: This is one of Engram’s strongest durable ideas. Public already preserves richer markdown memory artifacts, but long-running decisions and repeated refinements would benefit from an optional stable thread key so related saves revise one conceptual thread instead of fragmenting across many files.
- **Recommendation**: prototype later
- **Impact**: high

### Finding 5: Engram’s search is intentionally simple: direct topic-key shortcut first, sanitized FTS5 second
- **Source**: [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L1462](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L1462); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L3382](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/store/store.go#L3382); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts#L482](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-search.ts#L482); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-context.ts#L1078](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/skills/system-spec-kit/mcp_server/handlers/memory-context.ts#L1078)
- **What it does**: If the query contains `/`, Engram tries direct `topic_key` lookup first and assigns those hits a dominant rank, then falls back to quoted FTS5 `MATCH` ordered by `fts.rank`. Public’s `memory_search` is much broader: vector + lexical + rerank + intent routing + session/causal boosts, while `memory_context` adds orchestration and graph-aware routing.
- **Why it matters for us**: Engram’s lexical path is not better than Public’s hybrid stack overall, but its exact-thread shortcut is useful. The idea to copy is the deterministic “if this looks like a thread key, bypass normal ranking,” not the FTS-only architecture.
- **Recommendation**: prototype later
- **Impact**: medium

### Finding 6: Agent-agnostic adoption is driven by setup/install code and hook-level protocol injection, not by core-store complexity
- **Source**: [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/setup/setup.go#L1](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/internal/setup/setup.go#L1); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/plugin/opencode/engram.ts#L1](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/plugin/opencode/engram.ts#L1); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/plugin/claude-code/scripts/session-start.sh#L1](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/plugin/claude-code/scripts/session-start.sh#L1); [/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/README.md#L45](/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.opencode/specs/system-spec-kit/999-hybrid-rag-fusion-upgrade/001-research-hybrid-rag-fusion-systems/001-engram-main/external/README.md#L45)
- **What it does**: `setup.go` writes/install-configures agent-specific MCP integrations for OpenCode, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex. The OpenCode adapter is explicitly “thin,” and the Claude session-start hook starts the server, creates a session, imports sync state, fetches context, and injects protocol text on startup.
- **Why it matters for us**: The strong pattern here is distribution discipline: keep setup friction low, keep hooks small, and keep behavioral protocol near the runtime seam. Public already supports more advanced runtime recovery, but Engram’s packaging is cleaner and easier to reason about.
- **Recommendation**: prototype later
- **Impact**: medium
